Flooding on the Hutuo River was harming Zhending. Qiyan argued that ennobling the river god as a marquis was misguided, sent an official rebuke, repaired the dikes, and dredged the choked channels until the floods subsided.

Flooding on the Hutuo River was harming Zhending. Qiyan proposed ennobling the river god as a marquis, sent an official rebuke, repaired the dikes, and dredged the choked channels until the floods subsided.
論封河神為侯爵 records proposing or discussing a marquisate; the original English invents that he judged the enfeoffment misguided.

The waters of the Hutuo River harmed Zhending; Qiyan argued that enfeoffing the river god as marquis was wrong, and sent an official communication to reprove it; he again repaired the dikes, dredged the choked and stagnant channels, and the flood harm then ceased.

The waters of the Hutuo River harmed Zhending; Qiyan argued for enfeoffing the river god as marquis, and sent an official communication to reprove it; he again repaired the dikes, dredged the choked and stagnant channels, and the flood harm then ceased.
論封 does not mean he argued the enfeoffment was wrong; that negation is added in English.

His great-grandfather Xin was the first to move the family to Liuyang, so Xuan was counted as a native of Liuyang.
曾大父 is great-grandfather (three generations up), not great-great-grandfather.

大司徒 is Grand Minister of Education (Situ), not grand preceptor (太師).

The posthumous office in the source is 大司徒, not 太師.

會福達魯花赤 is darughachi of Huifu, not the ethnonym Qarachu.

At the start of the renewed Zhizhi era, Han Gongpu of Changlu triggered a major case over weapons found in his home. It swept through the censorate and secretariat, and many officials fell on corruption charges, but Youren's name was never implicated, which only sharpened the resentment against him.

重紀至元 is the renewed Zhiyuan era, not Zhizhi.
